document.title: Drive UI location from the URL hash
document.summary: The UI reads and writes `window.location.hash`. `#overview`, `#group/<id>`, `#unassigned`, and `#lockfiles` name the place. Empty or unknown hashes fall back to the old default. The first write and a dead hash use `replaceState`. A live hop uses `pushState`. Theme and viewed files stay in sessionStorage. Serve and export still share one UI shell. After rebase onto main, lookFor owner hops, header pager, and story Depends on go through the same selection write.
document.why: [#78](source:s1) wants the current place in the URL, so share, refresh, Back, and GitHub Pages match `comprehende serve`.

sources.title: URL hash-based routing (serve + export)
sources.gist: Store UI location in the URL hash for serve and GitHub Pages export. Empty hash keeps the current default. Header, story, and lookFor hops must stay coherent with that hash.

lookFor: Share a `#group/<id>` URL. The UI opens that group, not Overview. [#78](source:s1).
Open a lookFor owner on Overview. The hash must move with that owner. [#78](source:s1).
Click Next group or press `[` / `]`. The hash must change. Back must return. [#78](source:s1).
Reload a GitHub Pages export on `#group/<id>`. The group must still be selected. [#78](source:s1).

groups.title: Hash is the stored place
groups.why: [#78](source:s1) wants the URL to name the current place, not sessionStorage.
groups.summary: `parseHash` and `serializeHash` map the four selection kinds to `#overview`, `#group/<id>`, `#unassigned`, and `#lockfiles`. Group ids are encoded. `selectionFromHash` returns the old default for empty or unknown hashes. `hashWriteMode` skips a no-op, replaces the first write and a dead hash, and pushes a live hop. Tests cover parse, serialize, serve vs Pages URLs, `[` / `]` push, and lookFor owner hops to `#group/login` or `#overview`.
lookFor: `#group/login` must survive a full page URL, not only `window.location.hash`. [#78](source:s1).
A lookFor owner hop to login must be a `push`, so Back can leave that group. [#78](source:s1).

groups.title: App reads and writes the hash
groups.why: The hash helpers do not talk to the window. The app must load from the hash, write on selection change, and apply Back.
groups.summary: `restoreSelection` now takes `window.location.hash`. A layout effect writes the hash with `history.replaceState` or `history.pushState`. `hashchange` and `popstate` call `selectFromNav`, so Back also clears lookFor highlight. `openLookFor` and `openSource` still call `selectWithMotion`, so lookFor, source, header pager, story Depends on, and `[` / `]` all write the hash.
lookFor: First paint must not add a history entry. Later hops must. [#78](source:s1).
Back from a lookFor jump must clear the highlighted claim. The hash apply uses `selectFromNav`. [#78](source:s1).

groups.title: README names the hashes; export stays one shell
groups.why: People who share a review need to know the hash names. Export must keep the same UI as serve.
groups.summary: README lists `#overview`, `#group/<id>`, `#unassigned`, and `#lockfiles`. The export test still asserts that serve and export return the same `index.html`.

commits.subject: Drive UI location from the URL hash
commits.author: Cursor Agent
commits.body:
Replace sessionStorage as the review route with `#overview`, `#group/<id>`, and the bucket hashes so serve and static export share the same view on refresh and shared links.

Co-authored-by: Máté Molnár <matemolnar8@users.noreply.github.com>
